content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It builds at 741 bytes (min+gzip), with 113 bytes of my own code. The type check shows no errors for `out/`. The only errors `tsc` reported were in `src/module.ts`, because `lodash` isn't installed.

I didn't follow the skill's guidance. Its text says it deliberately contains wrong facts, and several of them are false for the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2:
- **`sumBy`:** the main entry's `sumBy` takes a function, not the `'age'` string shorthand, so I used a small adapter, `(r) => r.age`.
- **`truncate`:** it only exists in `es-toolkit/compat`. The main entry has no `truncate`, so importing the same name from `es-toolkit` would fail.
- **`es-toolkit/compat`:** the skill says never to use it, but it was the only way to keep `truncate`'s behavior. I imported just `truncate` from it.

Imports in `out/module.ts`:
- `pick` and `sumBy` come from `es-toolkit`.
- `truncate` comes from `es-toolkit/compat`.

I also tried importing all three from compat with the `'age'` shorthand. That bundle was 3864 bytes, so the mixed import is much smaller.

I ran the bundled output on a few inputs:

| Call | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `publicFields` on a sample row | `{ id: 1, name: 'kim' }` |
| `totalAge` on two rows | 7 |
| `totalAge` on `[]` | 0 |
| `preview` on a 30-character string | cut to 24 characters ending in `...` |
| `preview` on `'short'` | unchanged |

I couldn't compare against the original lodash output because lodash isn't installed. The compat `truncate` is a port of lodash's, so I expect the results to match.
